how.q: Run the merge queue on a fresh machine?
how.a: Sign in to GitHub with the CLI, then run the merge queue script with the pull request number. It merges a green pull request without a re-run when main moved only outside its classes, and updates the branch otherwise.

how.q: Stage and upload a batch of files?
how.a: Put the files in the staging folder and run the upload script. It copies them to object storage and records each upload in the bucket's log, which is the only record kept.
Put one seed file per unit in the seed folder, open a pull request, and run the importer after it merges. The importer reads the folder and writes to the database through the app.

Create the key in the service's dashboard, store it in the password manager under the project's entry, set it in the environment, and add a line to the setup document. The card for that service turns ready on its own.
Generate a new key, set it alongside the old one for a day so open sessions keep working, then remove the old one. Record the date in the setup document.
Run the nightly backup job from the Actions tab with the manual trigger. It writes a dated dump to the backup bucket.
Nothing in this project deletes. Move files to the archive folder in storage; a nightly job moves anything older than a year there on its own.

how.q: Confirm a claim on an item?
how.a: Open the item in the admin, check the proof the claimant sent against the record, and press confirm. The claimant gets an email and the item shows them as the holder.
Reports arrive as issues labeled report. Reply on the issue, change what needs changing in a pull request, and close the issue; the reporter gets the reply by email.

when.q: A form is sent by a machine?
when.a: The bot check rejects it before the app sees it and the sender gets a plain message asking them to try again. Nothing is stored.
The image cache serves them without touching the app. Known crawlers are rate limited at the edge; the originals are never served directly.
The payment provider retries on its own schedule and sends an event each time. The app marks the account as past due after the last retry and emails the person a link to update their card.
The provider emails the owner at eighty percent. The nightly audit comments on the tracking issue when the bucket passes ninety percent.
Jobs fall through to the hosted runner in the same group, more slowly. Nothing waits forever; a job that cannot start in an hour fails and the merge queue tries again later.
The full run opens an issue labeled ci-red. Nothing else merges until it is closed. The nightly audit keeps mentioning it while it is open.
Confirm who they are the same way as a claim, then move the item aside in the admin. It leaves public view at once and stays in the archive, which is never deleted.
